translations.adaptations: Scoped to ordinary amino-acid lookup with non-position-specific matrix, the standard tblastn protein word-finder path. Typed lookup/scanner references replace the untyped wrapper; PSSM, RPS and compressed-AA branches are excluded. Preserve original control flow, score/coordinate comparisons, hit order, diagonal mutations and output/status handling. ProteinSequence exposes the original sequence-block sequence pointer and logical length as a borrowed slice/length view. Normal Rust memory ownership replaces C pointer allocation. AminoAcidSubject carries sequence/ranges for the existing scanner; explicit subject_length retains logical length independently of readable physical tail storage. Reuse original typed scanner callback, BlastExtendWord/packed signed31+flag diagonal cells, per-context cutoffs, hit storage, exit and statistics helpers. Preserve mixed unsigned query/subject subtraction and promotions with explicit wrapping u32 arithmetic. Assert buffer can hold the longest chain to enforce the original caller requirement and avoid nonprogress on an undersized buffer. Caller retains responsibility for subject/frame preparation and per-subject hit-list reset. Preserve multiple_hits dispatch and unconditional score sort after the selected finder returns. Sorting retains the established comparator-key semantics, including platform-unspecified ties.

integration.entry_point: blast_aa_word_finder(subject: &AminoAcidSubject, subject_length: i32, query: &ProteinSequence, query_info: &BlastQueryInfo, lookup: &BlastAaLookupTable, matrix: &[Vec<i32>], word_params: &BlastInitialWordParameters, ewp: &mut BlastExtendWord, offset_pairs: &mut [BlastOffsetPair], offset_array_size: i32, init_hitlist: &mut BlastInitHitList, ungapped_stats: Option<&mut BlastUngappedStats>) -> i16
frontend_wiring: ProteinSequence {sequence, length} carries logical query length separately from a potentially padded slice.

Pass one translated nucleotide subject frame at a time as NCBIstdaa with logical protein length and frame-coordinate half-open seq_ranges. Keep frame metadata outside this helper exactly as the C pipeline does; convert accepted HSP frame coordinates later.
Use a diagonal array, not a diagonal hash, and keep original extension-state lifetime across subject calls. Default tblastn options produce window40/multiple_hits=true.
Select the existing AA scanner callback before calling, and allocate at least longest_chain pairs (the original recommended 4096+longest_chain is also suitable).
Reset the initial-hit list before each frame/subject call as original engine caller does; the finder itself does not reset it.

Default engine frontend should skip translated subjects shorter than the word size; TwoHit retains the original initial clamp/readable-word precondition. The underlying scanner needs readable physical storage through any scan word.
Per-context cutoff/xdrop values and query context offsets must already be populated by translated statistical setup.
integration.scope: Ordinary non-PSSM protein lookup and ungapped extension only. Full tblastn subject translation, gapped scoring, traceback, composition adjustment and frame coordinate conversion remain pipeline work.
